nodes.name: Coordination Polymer Formation
nodes.procedure: Adding 4,4'-bipyridine ligand into solution containing transition metal ions (Ni:Fe:Co:Mn:Cr:Zn = 0.23:0.14:0.20:0.11:0.18:0.15) to synthesize Cl-HECP precipitates in ethanol solution.
nodes.source_text: we synthesized Cl-HECP (Ni_{2.9}Fe_{1.5}Co_{2.2}Mn_{1.21}Cr_{0.9}Zn_{1.6}) precipitates as an example by adding the 4,4'-bipyridine ligand into a solution containing various transition metal ions: Ni:Fe:Co:Mn:Cr:Zn = 0.23:0.14:0.20:0.11:0.18:0.15... Cl-HECP (Ni_{3.2}Fe_{1.2}Co_{0.71}Mn_{0.98}Cr_{1.06}Zn_{1.45}) was synthesized in an ethanol solution

nodes.name: Cl-to-SCN Anion Exchange
nodes.procedure: Cl-HECP nanoparticles coated onto nickel electrode and immersed in KSCN solution for 24 h. During this treatment process, Cl-HECP nanoparticles underwent Cl-to-SCN anion exchange reaction and converted into SCN-HECP with nanobelt morphology.

unit_operations.name: Electrode Coating
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Cl-HECP nanoparticles were then coated onto a nickel electrode

unit_operations.name: Anion Exchange
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: subsequently immersed in a KSCN solution for 24 h. During this treatment process, the Cl-HECP nanoparticles underwent a Cl-to-SCN anion exchange reaction

nodes.source_text: These Cl-HECP nanoparticles were then coated onto a nickel electrode and subsequently immersed in a KSCN solution for 24 h. During this treatment process, the Cl-HECP nanoparticles underwent a Cl-to-SCN anion exchange reaction and were converted into an SCN-HECP with a nanobelt morphology

nodes.name: Electrochemical Activation
nodes.procedure: SCN-HECP nanobelts converted into 2D amorphous high-entropy oxyhydroxide electrocatalysts via in situ electrochemical activation through crystalline-to-amorphous transformation process in KOH solution using cyclic voltammetry between 1.0 and 1.7 V vs RHE.
nodes.source_text: these crystalline SCN-CP nanobelts were converted into 2D amorphous oxyhydroxide electrocatalysts via an in situ electrochemical activation approach in a KOH solution... sweeping cyclic voltammetry (CV) between 1.0 and 1.7 V versus a reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE)

nodes.characterization_summary: SCN-HECP nanobelt shows feather-like morphology with bilateral symmetry at ~145° angle.
nodes.evidence_snippet: cryo-TEM imaging further revealed that the distinct feather-like morphology of this SCN-HECP nanobelt presented a bilateral symmetry structure with an angle of approximately 145° between the two symmetrical components (Figure 2a).

properties.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy image showing purple-colored elongated nanostructures with label 'Ni'
properties.features: elongated, sheet-like or rod-like morphology, high contrast

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms SCN-HECP has single-crystal structure along [010] direction with twin structure along [001] axis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern suggested that this SCN-HECP nanobelt had an obvious single-crystal structure along its [010] direction (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SCN-HECP shows (001) lattice spacing 1.14 nm and (100) lattice spacing 1.12 nm along [010] direction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The figure clearly shows two-dimensional (001) and (100) lattices along the [010] crystal direction, with spacings of 1.14 and 1.12 nm, respectively (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows uniform spatial distribution of Ni, Fe, Co, Mn, Cr, Zn in SCN-HECP without elemental segregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping demonstrated that this as-prepared SCN-HECP nanobelt featured a uniform spatial distribution of various transition metal elements

nodes.characterization_summary: 2D AHE shows porous structure; SAED pattern (inset) reveals broad diffuse halo ring confirming amorphous nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the cryo-TEM image clearly shows the porous structure of the amorphous high-entropy nanobelt (Figure 2e), which is also consistent with the 3D-scanned AFM results. The SAED pattern revealed a broad and diffuse halo ring (inset in Figure 2e)

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image and elemental mapping of 2D AHE show uniform uncorrelated spatial distribution of metal elements without phase separation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping revealed a uniform and uncorrelated spatial distribution of metal elements within the 2D AHE, devoid of any phase separation or heterogeneity

nodes.characterization_summary: 2D AHE oxidation states: Ni +2.8, Fe +3.0, Co +2.8, Mn +3.6, Cr +5.3, Zn +2.0 from K-edge XANES analysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: We calculated the fitted average oxidation states of the 2D AHE from XANES analysis ... approximately +2.8 for Ni, +3.0 for Fe, +2.8 for Co, +3.6 for Mn, +5.3 for Cr, and +2.0 for Zn (Figure 2g-l).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM imaging reveals SCN-HECP nanobelt has 2D layered structure with layer thickness of approximately 1.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging revealed that this SCN-HECP nanobelt exhibited a 2D layered structure ... with a layer thickness of approximately 1.5 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: Optimal 2D AHE shows typical amorphous structure without lattice fringes in cryo-HRTEM image and SAED pattern.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cryo-HRTEM image and SAED pattern suggested that the optimal 2D AHE had a typical amorphous structure without showing any lattice fringes.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge-transfer resistance of optimal 2D AHE is 4.92 Ω, lower than commercial anode (15.74 Ω).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The charge-transfer resistance of 2D AHE (4.92Ω) was significantly lower than that of the commercial OER anode (15.74Ω)

nodes.characterization_summary: CV in non-Faraday region gives C_dl of optimal 2D AHE as 2.5 mF cm⁻², higher than commercial anode (1.4 mF cm⁻²).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The C_dl value of 2D AHE is 2.5 mF cm⁻², higher than that of the commercial OER anode (1.4 mF cm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines compositions of 252 AHE samples and optimal AHE (Ni₂.₂Fe₁.₀Co₀.₁₅Mn₀.₂₃Cr₀.₀₈Zn₀.₁₅); measures low metal ion dissolution during stability tests.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transition metal ion compositions of 252 sets of AHE samples were determined via inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) analysis (Table S2).
